message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with the **Compute Engine API** enabled.  
> * Your project must have a **GPU quota** for the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator in the zone you choose.  
> * The `gcloud` SDK must be installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --zone us-central1-a \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure
```

### Explanation

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The GCP zone where the instance will live. Replace `us-central1-a` with your preferred zone. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM – enough for most workloads. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. Adjust size/type as needed. |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host machine is rebooted for maintenance, the VM will be terminated (not stopped). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the VM if it crashes. |

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a script or Terraform), here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470" }
    ]
  },
  "maintenancePolicy": "TERMINATE",
  "restartOnFailure": true
}
```

### How to POST

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `PROJECT_ID` with your actual project ID and adjust the zone (`us-central1-a`) if needed.

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Enable GPU Quota** – Check that `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is available in your zone.  
2. **Choose Zone** – GPU availability varies by zone.  
3. **Machine Type** – Pick a type that matches your CPU/RAM needs.  
4. **Boot Disk** – SSD is recommended for GPU workloads.  
5. **Startup Script** – Optional but handy for installing NVIDIA drivers automatically.  

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 GPU and its driver version. Happy computing!
